content: I mentioned at the packathon today that maybe we should make a tau ceti roadmap for the dim 8 and 24 cases and use this as the next stage in the code cleanup. What do people think about this?

I have multiple thoughts:

  • For cleanup purpose, especially for dimension 8, maybe we can keep working on our repository?
  • For dimension 24 (by Gauss), there are some definitions that worth upstreaming, such as theta series of lattice, spherical code and some polynomial families related to it (all used to prove uniqueness, which is not the main result of Cohn-Kumar-Miller-Radchenko-Viazovska, but other papers by different authors). Maybe we can start with these first (basically things under Uniqueness directory of Gauss formalization)

Yeah I don't think putting dim 8 in Tau Ceti is helpful at this stage - I think Tau Ceti has already rejected certain proposals / blueprints because there's an existing project for them. I view one of the aims of the cleanup to be to better understand the proof and better understand how it should be formalised, and I don't think Tau Ceti aims to do either of those

The stuff I've been adding to Tau ceti is all already done in aintlib and that's not been a problem, but perhaps this case is different. I just saw that the code I've already added got much nicer so I thought it would be a good experiment here. But maybe we don't do dim 8, I don't have strong feelings about this. What about dim 24?

For dimension 24, I think adding stuffs related to the uniqueness results would be interesting. If these are done, then there can be some follow-up project that people can do on top of it, such as optimal kissing numbers in certain dimensions. As far as I remember, Gauss formalization have a proof of transformation law for theta series of Leech lattice (using Poisson summation), which should be easily generalizable to arbitrary unimodular even lattices, so that we can get more examples of modular forms (of level 1, weight =d/2=d/2=d/2).

For dimension 8, another possible direction is to add things related to Viazovska's "original" proof, i.e. what is written in the Annals paper. The original proof uses certain Fourier coefficient bounds of meromorphic modular forms that comes from Maass-Poincare series and Rademacher type formula + Kloosterman sum bound (I'm not 100% sure about this, which I vaguely remember from Bruinier's book on Borcherd lift that is cited in the paper). Formalizing this might not contribute much to sphere packing project (since we're following different approach), but I thing these are interesting topics to formalize.

My suggestion is that Tau Ceti roadmaps (and then PRs) for any reusable components from sphere packing would be wonderful, but the material that is "specific to the end result" should not go to Tau Ceti.
